title: The Eagle
sub: Six lines, and every one of them a picture. Each level gives you a little less, so by the last one you are saying it on your own.
source: Alfred, Lord Tennyson, 1851. Out of copyright.

lines.t: He clasps the crag with crooked hands;
Close to the sun in lonely lands,
Ring’d with the azure world, he stands.
The wrinkled sea beneath him crawls;
He watches from his mountain walls,
And like a thunderbolt he falls.

levels.name: Last words
levels.tag: One blank at the end of each line
levels.blurb: The whole poem is in front of you. Only the last word of each line is missing — and hands, lands and stands all rhyme, which helps.

levels.name: First words
levels.tag: One blank at the start of each line
levels.blurb: Now the first word of each line is gone. Starting a line is the bit people get stuck on when they stand up to recite.

levels.name: Half gone
levels.blurb: About half the words are away now, spread through the poem. The shape of it is still there to lean on.

levels.name: Line by line
levels.blurb: One whole line at a time, with the rest of the poem still on the page around it.

levels.name: By heart
levels.blurb: No words on the screen at all. A picture for each line, and you say it from memory.
